meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Who decided on it?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Owen found out on his phone, in the middle of class. What is your basis for the zero?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Students misquote plays all the time. Why is that anything more than a bad citation?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire's case is the reason I'll be in the principal's office after this. Now, the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing is on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record, and she is heading to the principal; that is not the fair outcome, which was a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in a single sentence and moved on, which earned a flat okay from her, because it answered the process failure she cared about most.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and the family history, which made her go cold and name the principal, and it came right after she had asked a fair question about the misquote that you left unanswered.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed far from that night, since you gave no times or late hours, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked why a misquote is more than a bad citation, answer with something she can check herself, such as how that line compares with Owen's other writing, instead of turning to her family.
